title: Handbook of Ancient Afro-Eurasian Economies
bookshelves: Category: Economics, Finance, Business and Management
summary: In the second volume a wide range of economic actors – from kings and armies to cities and producers – are discussed within different imperial settings as well as the tools which enabled and constrained economic outcomes. A central focus are nodes of consumption that are visible in the archaeological and textual records of royal capitals, cities, religious centers, and armies that were stationed in imperial frontier zones.
